latest_nl_proof:
If m=0, then u is empty and -u is also empty, and the statement gives U_0(empty)=1. Hence U_0(u)=U_0(-u).

Now assume m>=1. For any sign sequence v of length m-1, let A(v) be the set of permutations b=(b_1,...,b_m) of {1,...,m} such that v_i(b_{i+1}-b_i)>0 for every i with 1<=i<=m-1. Then U_m(v)=|A(v)| by definition.

Define a map T on the set of all permutations of {1,...,m} by
T(b_1,...,b_m)=(m+1-b_1,\dots,m+1-b_m).
Because the map x↦m+1-x is a bijection from {1,...,m} to itself, T sends permutations to permutations. Also T is an involution, since applying it twice gives back the original permutation.

Take any b=(b_1,...,b_m) in A(u), and write c=T(b). For each i with 1<=i<=m-1,
c_{i+1}-c_i=(m+1-b_{i+1})-(m+1-b_i)=-(b_{i+1}-b_i).
Therefore
(-u_i)(c_{i+1}-c_i)=(-u_i)(-(b_{i+1}-b_i))=u_i(b_{i+1}-b_i)>0.
So c belongs to A(-u). Thus T maps A(u) into A(-u).

The same computation, with -u in place of u, shows that if c is in A(-u), then T(c) is in A(u). Since T is its own inverse, T restricts to a bijection between A(u) and A(-u). Hence
U_m(u)=|A(u)|=|A(-u)|=U_m(-u).

For the special case of alternating patterns, alt_m^- is the componentwise negative of alt_m^+ (and when m<=1 both are empty), so the equality just proved gives
U_m(alt_m^+)=U_m(-alt_m^+)=U_m(alt_m^-).
This proves the lemma.
role_in_parent: Ensures that both alternating orientations have the same count, so one alternating-count sequence E_m suffices for both parities.
statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 0, and let u = (u_1,...,u_{m-1}) be a sign sequence with each u_i in {+1,-1}; when m <= 1 this sequence is empty. For any sign sequence v of the same length, define U_m(v) to be the number of permutations (b_1,...,b_m) of {1,...,m} satisfying v_i * (b_{i+1} - b_i) > 0 for all 1 <= i <= m-1, and set U_0(empty) = 1. Let -u denote the sign sequence (-u_1,...,-u_{m-1}). Then U_m(u) = U_m(-u). In particular, if alt_m^+ = (+1,-1,+1,-1,...) and alt_m^- = (-1,+1,-1,+1,...) are the two alternating sign sequences of length m-1, then U_m(alt_m^+) = U_m(alt_m^-).

domain_restrictions: m must be a nonnegative integer.
Each entry of u and v must be either plus one or minus one.
When m is 0 or 1, the sequence u is empty.
v must have the same length as u.
b must be a permutation of 1 through m, meaning it lists each integer from 1 to m exactly once.
The inequality constraint is required for every i from 1 to m minus 1.
The definition includes the special value U_0 of the empty sequence equal to 1.
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every nonnegative integer m and every sign sequence u of length m minus 1, the number of permutations of {1,...,m} whose adjacent differences match the sign pattern u is unchanged when every sign in the pattern is flipped. Equivalently, the count for u equals the count for -u. As a special case, the two alternating sign patterns of length m minus 1 give the same count.
quantifier_order: Fix a sign sequence u of length m minus 1 with entries plus one or minus one; if m is 0 or 1, this sequence is empty.

For any sign sequence v of the same length, define U_m(v) as the number of permutations b of {1,...,m} such that for every index i from 1 to m minus 1, v_i times the difference b_{i+1} minus b_i is positive.
The theorem asserts that U_m(u) equals U_m of the sign-flipped sequence -u.
In particular, the same equality holds for the two alternating sign sequences alt_m^+ and alt_m^- of length m minus 1.

variables.domain: sequences of length m minus 1 with entries plus one or minus one
variables.name: u

variables.domain: sequences of the same length as u with entries plus one or minus one
variables.name: v
variables.role: arbitrary sign pattern used in the definition of U_m

variables.name: b
variables.role: counted object in the definition of U_m

variables.name: i
variables.role: adjacency index in the inequality constraints

witness_dependencies: There is no existential witness in the theorem statement itself; the only existentially quantified objects are the permutations counted in the definition of U_m(v).
Any counted permutation b depends on both m and the chosen sign sequence v.
The sign-flipped sequence -u is determined componentwise by u and has the same length as u.
